# templates/v1

An extension that serves pages of its own (tokens' OAuth sign-in, consent and MFA screens) keeps them as a set of Go
`html/template` files, usually embedded in the binary. A project themes them by ejecting the set and editing its copy:
any file it has replaces the built-in one, and anything it leaves out falls back. The format is always Go templates,
so the built-in pages and the ejected ones are the same files.

A set is every `*.tpl` file in an `fs.FS`, at any depth. Each file is one template named by its path without `.tpl`
(`signin`, `parts/head`), so pages include shared pieces with `{{template "parts/head" .}}`.

An app service contract, one provider ([templates.go](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/templates/v1/templates.go)).

## Use

Add your set in `Register`, then render a page through the provider at request time, falling back to your own set
when nothing provides the contract:

```go
//go:embed templates/oauth
var oauthFiles embed.FS

files, _ := fs.Sub(oauthFiles, "templates/oauth")
templatesv1.Add(app, "oauth", files)

// in a handler
if t, ok := templatesv1.Contract.Of(app); ok {
	return t.Render(e, "oauth", "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
}
set, err := templatesv1.Parse(files, nil)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
return templatesv1.Write(e, set, "signin", http.StatusOK, data)
```

Declare the contract in `WorksWith`. Pass anything that must not be escaped (ready-made HTML) as `template.HTML`.

## Provide

Implement `templatesv1.Templates` (`Render`, `Eject`) and provide it in `Register`. Read the sets with
`templatesv1.Set` and `templatesv1.Names`, and build each page with `templatesv1.Parse(set, projectCopy)` and
`templatesv1.Write`, so every provider renders the same way:

```go
templatesv1.Contract.Provide(app, myTemplates)
```
